title: Lake District travel writing: Penrith to Pooley Bridge
text: From Penrith two roads lead to Pooley Bridge, about six miles distant, which spans the Eamont just at its issue from Ulleswater.
source_note: Short nineteenth-century Lake District travel-writing example used in the Spatial Narratives project teaching materials. Verify the exact CLDW source/edition citation before final public release.

title: Synthetic oral-history Q/A journey
text:
Q: Where did you live before the war?
A: We lived in Amsterdam near my mother's family. Later we were deported by train to Auschwitz. I remember being very cold.
Q: What happened after liberation?
A: I travelled to London and found my brother there.
source_note: Instructor-created synthetic example. It is not a quotation from a survivor testimony.

title: Ambiguous place resolution
text: After university I left Cambridge and travelled to London, where I stayed for several months.

title: Historical place-name caution
text: In 1938 our family lived in Czechoslovakia. Years later I described the region using the names I knew at the time.

title: Relational and non-cartographic space
text: We left the village before dawn and hid in the woods beyond the river. The nearest road was somewhere to our left, but we avoided it.
